lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Mar 2019 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Coordinated the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations and prepares the forecast pack for each meeting.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Remove the date of birth.
items.because: It is not needed for a typical résumé and can introduce irrelevant bias.

items.says: Remove nationality unless an application specifically asks for it.
items.because: Work authorization, if relevant, should be addressed directly in the application process.

items.says: Check that the LinkedIn-style URL leads to a complete, current profile.
Consider adding a specific target-role positioning line or summary.
items.because: Without one, a recruiter must infer the target role from the experience.

items.says: Clarify the MBA’s status if submitting the résumé after June 2025.
items.because: The listed end date has passed, but the résumé does not say whether the degree was completed.

items.says: Clarify whether the 35% conversion improvement is relative growth or percentage points.
items.because: The result needs enough measurement context to be credible.

items.says: Support the implied causal link between replacing the flow and improved conversion.
items.because: “After replacing” implies causation.

items.says: Make the dispute self-service feature’s result or purpose clearer.
items.because: The bullet emphasizes process more than impact.

items.says: Be more precise about your role versus the team’s.
Clarify how the $1.1 million estimate was calculated and what period or population it covers.
items.because: The estimate drove a roadmap decision.

items.says: Clarify the scope of the open-ticket queue.
Clarify whether you closed tickets personally or coordinated their resolution.
Add a finding from the onboarding comparison or remove the method-only bullet.
items.because: It gives no result and may add no evidence beyond the later onboarding bullet.

items.says: Do not rely on the opt-in comparison alone to establish causation.
items.because: Merchants who opted in may differ from those who stayed on the old flow.

items.says: Make sure the onboarding result is not presented as applying to all merchants.
items.because: The result came from a pilot region.

items.says: Move the strongest Harbor achievements earlier in the role.
items.because: The onboarding result and discovery work are more persuasive than a method-only bullet.

items.says: Reduce overlap among the six Harbor bullets.
items.because: The checkout, onboarding and measurement bullets should read as distinct accomplishments.

items.says: Do not present the weather-adjusted late-delivery rate as an operational improvement.
items.because: Excluding delayed shipments can improve the reported rate without improving actual delivery performance.

items.says: Clarify the measurement period or comparison basis for the 30% reduction in pick errors.
Fix the shift from past to present tense in the S&OP bullet.
items.because: “Coordinated” and “prepares” make the timing inconsistent.

items.says: Include the S&OP work’s outcome or decision impact if available.
items.because: The bullet mainly lists responsibilities.

items.says: Clarify whether the 1,800 driver hours are measured savings or an estimate.
Clarify the period underlying the annual savings figure.
Distinguish students who had access to the app from those who used it.
items.because: “Launched…to 3,100 students” does not make that distinction.

items.says: Clarify the timeframe and counting method for the 9 tonnes of food.
Define “weekly active users” and clarify whether the compared periods are equivalent.
Clarify what the 95% pickup-slot rate measures.
Clarify whether the reduction in staff cover shifts occurred over the same period.
Add the working sessions’ outcome or your contribution to a decision.
items.because: The bullet states a responsibility rather than an accomplishment.

items.says: Clarify your role in mapping intake and shortening the form.
items.because: The passive voice obscures your contribution.

items.says: Show whether the shortened form measurably improved intake.
items.because: Saying the changes were adopted does not show their effect.

items.says: Remove or correct the merchant-payment result under the hospital practicum.
items.because: It does not fit a hospital scheduling project and closely repeats the Harbor onboarding achievement.

items.says: Expand the skills section selectively with substantiated capabilities.
items.because: It is thin compared with the claimed product work.

items.says: Make the skills groupings more reflective of the target role.
items.because: The categories are broad and do not show the depth of analytics or experimentation experience.

items.says: Be ready to explain what the listed A/B testing experience involved.
items.because: The measurement bullet describes a non-randomized opt-in comparison.
